notes.1:
Welcome

Welcome to PyPDFPresenter. This demo introduces a simple workflow for presenting PDF slides with a separate audience window. Everything runs locally.

Start the presentation with F5, then use the arrow keys to move through the deck. The audience sees only the slide. These notes stay in the presenter window.
notes.2:
Two views, one story

Explain the difference between the audience window and the presenter workspace. The current slide is shown alongside your speaker notes and a preview of the next page.

Choose a preview layout that matches your screen. Notes can sit beside the current slide, with the next slide below either area. The bottom layout also previews the next page of notes.
notes.3:
Notes that work for you

This page is a good place to demonstrate JSON speaker notes. Increase the font size to make the text comfortable to read.

The text is protected by default. Choose Edit notes to make a change, then Finish editing to return to reading. Text and font changes are saved automatically. Each entry belongs to a physical PDF page, including individual builds.
notes.4:
Keep the room focused

Turn on the laser pointer with L and move the mouse over the current slide. The audience window follows the same position.

Press B to black out the audience screen. Use Clean View to hide the header and the lower toolbar while keeping navigation and timing controls available. Click Clean View again to restore the controls.
notes.5:
Embedded video

This slide contains an original six-second animation as an embedded MP4. Press V, or click its region on the slide, to play or pause it.

The animation is extracted from this PDF and shown in place. No external viewer or internet connection is needed. Move to another page to stop playback. You can also enable Auto-play videos and return to this slide.
notes.6:
Ready for your next talk

Summarize the workflow: open a PDF, load or create JSON notes, choose the audience display, and start presenting.

This repository includes both a slide-only PDF with JSON notes and a wide presenter PDF with notes on the right. Try both to compare the workflows. The source and media assets are included, so you can edit and rebuild the example with pdfLaTeX.
